name: scene palette sets
rule: one backdrop shared by both layers, 4 background palettes of 3 entries on 16x16 areas, 4 sprite palettes of 3 entries plus transparency on 8x8 tiles, and 4 reserved hero palettes of 3; every entry is a data/nes_palette.json entry number, every entry usable
hero_rule: ART-BIBLE.md RULE 0 point 3: 4 reserved hero palettes of 3 colours each, 1 dark outline, 1 mid body, 1 accent; fixed, and changed only here
master_source: tools/art/nes_palette_build.py, cited to NESdev and 8bitphoto in knowledge/ART-BIBLE.md
notes: A scene's set is written down before the art is made (RULE 0 point 1) and named in the card and the output manifest of every concept round (RULE 0 point 6).
background and sprites are lists of 4 palettes of 3, in the order the PPU selects them: the first is palette 0, so entry 0 of background palette 0 is the backdrop.
heroes true means the scene also carries the 4 reserved hero palettes, so a character concept is quantised against the colours it will really ship with.

party_cast true means the scene draws the party, so its 4 sprite palettes ARE the 4 reserved hero palettes: they replace the scene's own sprite rows instead of adding to them, because the PPU has 4 sprite palettes and a frame has nowhere to put a fifth (knowledge/PALETTE-RULINGS-2026-10-25.md section 7.1, card t_c93a983f). A scene without the flag keeps its own 4 sprite rows, so the towns, the ship, the title, the icons, the sea and the ui scene are unchanged; the four battle strips carry it and nothing else does.
gate true means tools/palette_synergy.py may fail the build on this scene; a scene with gate false still reports its failing pairs, and gamedev decides when it becomes gated.

Generated by tools/scene_palette_set.py build --write from data/palettes/scene_*.json. Do not hand edit a scene's numbers here: edit the per scene file or the art, then rebuild, so the numbers stay derived from something measured.

bands.note: One background palette per 16 px row band, top to bottom (tools/art/title_bands.py). The title only scrolls along x, so a screen band always takes its pixels from the same band of a strip, and this plan holds at every camera position, not just at the one a capture happens to catch. The sky is two palettes because the gold of the logo and the white of the clouds cannot share three entries. The ground is two palettes that differ only in their accent: bands 8-11 spend the lit green of the fields, bands 12-14 the teal of the road. Both ground palettes carry $0B the dark green and $20 the white, which is why the window, the font, the cursor and the copyright line cross the boundary between them without changing a pixel.

band_sprites._note: Which palette each sprite sheet is drawn inside, so that a photograph of the finished frame can be judged by the same three-entry rule the background is judged by: the checker has no sprite mask, so a sprite pixel that left its band palette would read as a fourth colour in that 16x16 area. A sheet that can touch two bands takes the colours those bands share, which is why the menu box, the font and the cursor name both ground palettes: the two of them share exactly the dark green and the white, which is all those three sheets spend. This is a compatibility pass, not the hardware rule: a sprite owns one of the four sprite palettes in "sprites" above. The fade twins, the intro's star sheet, the Big Ben opening frame and the retired cast are not here: the intro is a different shot with its own fade art, and giving it a band plan of its own is a separate card.

the sprites_v2 contact sheet, the whole v2 cast read against one ground at a time
audit.exempt: a contact sheet is a diagnostic, not a cast: it draws the whole v2 roster in one image, so no single palette set can carry it and a cast check on it would say nothing. It is also a BY PRODUCT: output/sprites_v2_sheet.png is gitignored, so no clean checkout reproduces it, and two generators write different content under the one name (tools/art/make_characters_v2.py measures 11 records on this machine, tools/art/make_title_rows_v2.py 3 on the far side). Card t_c93a983f, ruling section 8 of knowledge/PALETTE-RULINGS-2026-10-25.md: when the file is absent the row reports NOT MEASURED with a printed line instead of refusing the run, and when it is present it is measured and reported advisory whatever it measures

audit.note: the deck strip is a battle screen, so it draws the same four 24x32 party slots at x=224 (data/ui_layouts.json) and its four sprite palettes are the four reserved hero triples; this row names the party's four battle sheets (card t_0949bd4e). The sailor fight cast this row named until 2026-10-25 is not drawn from a sprite palette on a strip that draws four heroes: ruling 7.5 makes the enemy background art, and sailor_battle.png and sailor_ow_v2.png stay judged where the ship draws them, on the ship row against ts_ship.png. The enemy that the tutorial fight does draw, navy_sailor.png, is now drawable as background art on this strip: its cells are bg2, and bg2 $00 $30 $02 plus the backdrop $0F carries its three colours whole (ruling section 15, card t_34b1d96a)

card t_1dc346b9 ruling 2026-10-25 named the ground: the ship tileset the room is built from is the authoritative ground for the ship cast, because a ground has to be something a tool can measure and a composed capture is not (output/ship_dialogue.png carries colours off the 2C02 palette, so the tool charges its failures to the sprite standing on it). ts_ship.png is authored inside the ship's four background palettes, so it measures clean and only the sprite's own pair rules can fail. Card t_a6a7a436 ruling section 17 recast the row and kept the placement card t_1dc346b9 gave it, [64, 64]: the cast is now the WALKING cast, the party's four walking sheets plus sailor_ow_v2.png, because a walking room draws walking sheets. Measured 2026-10-25 at --at 64,64 against the four rows this file now carries: hadrian_ow_v2, konrad_ow_v2, zander_ow_v2, percy_ow_v2 and sailor_ow_v2 each fit exactly one row and read 0 failing pairs and 0 uncovered 8x8 tiles (32 inked each), hadrian on sp0, percy on sp1, zander on sp2, konrad on sp3, and the sailor on sp1 beside percy. sailor_battle.png came off this row: it is a 168x32 seven frame BATTLE sheet, no encounter draws it (data/encounters/all.json tutorial_sailors is navy_sailor), pp_overworld draws exactly two sheets (zander_ow_v2 for the hero and sailor_ow_v2 for a sailor actor) and it is neither, and under the four walking rows 40 of its 72 inked 8x8 tiles are uncovered by any row, against 0 of 72 under the old rows. Its ground is card t_0b9c2faf. The capture stays what it is, the dialogue screen that ships; it is no longer named as a ground.

card t_dec4e92c ruling 2026-10-25: the party's four walking sheets are judged on the frame tools/art/make_exterior_maps.py composes at this map's spawn, NOT on game/sprites_src/env/ts_exterior.png. The atlas spends FIVE background palettes (bg0_stone, bg1_brick, bg2_green, bg3_water, bg4_red) and a scene spends four, so as a ground it reports 7 palette_count problems here and can never measure clean, which is the one thing card t_1dc346b9 asks of a ground; the ship can use its tileset because ts_ship.png spends four and measures 0. This frame is built tile by tile from that atlas under the four group budget the generator enforces on itself, measures 0 background problems against this scene's four rows, is reproduced byte for byte by a rerun of the generator, and is the ground the party stands on at spawn tile 17,18 (256x240 crop x0 9, y0 11, spawn tile at 128,112). Measured 2026-10-25 at --at 128,112, after sp0 was solved to $00 $0F $30 (hadrian) and sp2 to $01 $11 $31 (zander): percy_ow_v2 PASS on cast (sp3), 8 white_blob; konrad_ow_v2 PASS on cast (sp1), 8 body_ground; zander_ow_v2 PASS on cast (sp2, solved here), 8 white_blob; hadrian_ow_v2 PASS on cast (sp0, solved here), 12 fails: white_blob 6, invisible 2, same_hue_row 2, body_ground 2. 36 failing pair(s) are the towns' light stone paving against the sheets' own bodies, not the cast: card t_454c1876 carries them (the walkable street surface is $10 #bcbcbc out of bg0_stone and the bodies are $30, $31 and $28). Closed on 2026-10-25: the paving, cobble, kerb, road, crossing and quay tiles now draw bg0_stone's M $00 #7c7c7c (0.202) and the shared backdrop $0F (0.000) and nothing else, because $10 and $30 sit above RULE 0 point 2's 0.25 light line and the party's bodies are $30, $31 and $28, so the street could never carry them. Re-measured on this same frame at --at 128,112: 0 failing pair(s), 0 cast problems, every sheet's body ($30 percy, $28 konrad, $31 zander, $30 hadrian) on ground $00,$0F, and tools/check_ts_exterior.py check 13 holds that for all 20 walkable tiles. The measurement above is kept as the record of what the light paving cost.
